data.title: Colgate outlines 1.5%-3% global category growth as costs peak in Q4 and logistics hit yearly high
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Colgate-Palmolive (CL) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We're clearly pleased to have delivered another quarter of solid top and bottom-line growth" and "organic sales growth in all four of our categories and four of our five divisions." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Noel Wallace).

  • "Base Business EPS came in ahead of our expectations even as we continue to increase our advertising" and "free cash flow up 7%, and we've returned $2.2 billion to shareholders year-to-date." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

  • "We also had strong contributions from our European markets where science-based premium innovation and our omnichannel generation model have led to record market shares" while "remain focused on executing our U.S. turnaround." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

  • "Material prices were roughly 300 basis points of a headwind" and "Funding the Growth drove over 290 basis points of offset to the material inflation." Quote (Chief Financial Officer Stanley Sutula).

  • "We guided for a margin to be up on a year-on-year basis, up from roughly flat previously" and "our commodities right now are largely locked in for Q4." Quote (CFO Sutula).

Outlook

  • "We won't be sharing guidance on '27 until the first quarter of next year" and "we expect the cost environment to continue through the fourth quarter and into the early part of next year." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

  • "We guided for a margin to be up on a year-on-year basis, up from roughly flat previously" and "we think we can expand our gross profit margin for the year." Quote (CFO Sutula).

  • "Tariffs would peak in the fourth quarter" and "FX is moving a little bit against us." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

Financial Results

  • "Free cash flow up 7%, and we've returned $2.2 billion to shareholders year-to-date." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

  • "Material prices were roughly 300 basis points of a headwind" with "Pricing... contributed 80 basis points" and "slight favorable from mix of about 20 basis points." Quote (CFO Sutula).

  • "Logistic costs have increased" and "our guidance for Q4 has the highest logistics cost quarter of the year, both in dollars and as a percent of sales." Quote (CFO Sutula).

  • "Hill's had a terrific quarter" with "the top line... 6.5% ex private label" and "gross margin up 170 basis points." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

  • "Overhead efficiencies" included "that 90 basis point improvement" in SG&A, and "SGPP... goes out through the end of 2028." Quote (CFO Sutula).

Q&A

  • Peter Galbo, BofA Securities: "some concern around what the elevated cost environment might mean for next year"; Chairman, CEO & President Wallace: "tariffs would peak in the fourth quarter" and "we'll provide guidance on '27 in the first quarter next year."

  • Dara Mohsenian, Morgan Stanley: "what drove the gross margin upside" and "the ROI behind" higher advertising; CFO Sutula: "Funding the Growth drove over 290 basis points" of offset; Chairman, CEO & President Wallace: "we feel very good about the ROIs that we're seeing."

  • Peter Grom, UBS: "unpack" Hill's momentum; Chairman, CEO & President Wallace: "in a tough environment with increased competition, we're seeing good market share growth" and called out "Prescription Diet Cat was up double digits."

  • Lauren Lieberman, Barclays: "overhead efficiencies" and run-rate; CFO Sutula: "it's really a combination of underlying productivity" and "SGPP... goes out through the end of 2028."

  • Stephen Powers, Deutsche Bank: Mexico slowdown and Brazil momentum; Chairman, CEO & President Wallace: "Mexico was hit with a difficult consumer backdrop" and "some very specific retailer challenges."

  • Filippo Falorni, Citi: U.S. toothpaste "early signs of improvement" and pricing environment; Chairman, CEO & President Wallace: "my expectation is that you'll have to see some pricing" and "we're restructuring to win that connection."

  • Bonnie Herzog, Goldman Sachs: consumption and category growth; Chairman, CEO & President Wallace: "We're seeing growth in the 1.5% to 3% globally" and "North America is where we're seeing the most pressure."

  • Olivia Tong Cheang, Raymond James: Hill's sustainability and margins; Chairman, CEO & President Wallace: "Fresh was insignificant in the quarter" and "a disciplined rollout"; CFO Sutula: "Hill's operating margin... is down just slightly" due to "investments into advertising."

  • Christopher Carey, Wells Fargo: U.S. de-stocking and APAC durability; Chairman, CEO & President Wallace: "we did not see any meaningful inventory destocking" and "Asia... roughly 5% organic."

  • Kaumil Gajrawala, Jefferies: cost curve visibility; CFO Sutula: "we're comfortable with our guidance" for Q4 and "I don't see the headwinds on commodities lightening up."

  • Robert Moskow, TD Cowen: inflation dollars and pricing timing; CFO Sutula: "roughly, it's still in the same original range of $300 million plus or minus"; Chairman, CEO & President Wallace: "the cost environment... will peak in the fourth quarter."

Sentiment Analysis

  • "some concern around what the elevated cost environment might mean for next year" and "a bit surprising" margin dynamics signaled slightly negative to pressing analyst tone, centered on costs, pricing durability, and North America. Quote (Peter Galbo, BofA Securities; Olivia Tong Cheang, Raymond James).

  • Management’s tone was slightly positive but guarded on external pressures, emphasizing controllable levers: "we have the levers and the flexibility" and "we're comfortable with our guidance" while reiterating that commodities and FX remain volatile. Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace; CFO Sutula).

  • Versus last quarter, management removed expectations of tariff refund help: "We had an insignificant amount of tariff refund" and "we're not anticipating in the fourth quarter to have any further tariff refunds." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The cost narrative stayed elevated, but the gross margin stance firmed: in Q2 the company said "We've increased our gross margin guidance to roughly flat for the year"; in Q3 it said "we guided for a margin to be up on a year-on-year basis, up from roughly flat previously." Quote (CFO Sutula).

  • U.S. retailer inventory commentary shifted: in Q2 management cited "inventory reductions from key retailers"; in Q3 it said "we did not see any meaningful inventory destocking." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

  • Shareholder returns and cash flow language changed as the year progressed: Q2 cited "free cash flow up 18%, and we returned $1.4 billion to shareholders"; Q3 cited "free cash flow up 7%" and "$2.2 billion" returned year-to-date. Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

  • Investor relations leadership transition advanced: Q3 noted "it's her last day, last earnings call with us" and "retire happily" after "103 quarters" for Hope Spiller. Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

Risks and Concerns

  • "Raw materials and freight and logistics... continues to operate in a really volatile environment" and "resins petrochemicals as well as pulp and paper" were cited as key cost headwinds, with mitigation tied to "Funding the Growth and SGPP." Quote (CFO Sutula).

  • "North America is where we're seeing the most pressure" and "China business continues to be challenged from a category standpoint." Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

  • "FX is moving a little bit against us" and "tariffs would peak in the fourth quarter" were highlighted as near-term uncertainties. Quote (Chairman, CEO & President Wallace).

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as another quarter of broad-based organic growth and margin resilience despite what it called a "stubborn" and "volatile" cost backdrop. The company emphasized pricing cadence, productivity programs (including Funding the Growth and SGPP), and scaling AI-enabled capabilities (including PromoAI) as its primary offsets while it continues a longer U.S. reset centered on premium innovation, go-to-market restructuring, and more targeted omnichannel demand generation. It also stressed that Q4 should mark peak tariffs and the year’s highest logistics costs, and reiterated that 2027 guidance will not be provided until Q1 2027.

data.title: TMX plans TSX Alpha extended hours in spring 2027 while guiding leverage peak at 3.1x-3.2x
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: TMX Group (X:CA) Q3 2026

Management View

  • CEO John McKenzie framed Q3 as “another excellent quarter for TMX,” citing “standout performances across the enterprise” and saying the company is delivering “double-digit year-over-year growth in overall revenue and adjusted earnings per share,” supported by “strong activity in key markets.” (CEO & Director John McKenzie)

  • McKenzie emphasized accelerated strategic execution and deal activity: “We closed two significant transactions during the third quarter, TMX Australia Exchange and RAFI Indices, and we are advancing on the approval process for the acquisition of Cboe Canada and the MEMX Group transaction.” He added, “Subsequent to the close of the quarter, we announced TMX VettaFi's acquisition of The SPADE Defense Indices.” (CEO & Director McKenzie)

  • McKenzie highlighted post-trade digitization as a near-term innovation focus, saying TMX is working to address “transactional frictions and the slow movement of funds,” and described an “aspiration… developing an institutional-grade digital asset infrastructure, integrated into a hybrid central securities depository.” (CEO & Director McKenzie)

  • CFO David Arnold reported: “Total revenue hit a record $491.1 million, up 17% compared to Q3 of last year.” He said diluted EPS “declined 12% due to noncash fair value adjustments on foreign exchange hedges as well as acquisition and intercompany financing related FX movements,” while “adjusted diluted earnings per share… grew 21% compared with Q3 of last year.” (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

Outlook

  • Management did not provide formal revenue or EPS guidance for upcoming quarters in the prepared remarks, but laid out several timeline- and target-driven initiatives. McKenzie said TMX “submitted our plan to launch extended hours on TSX Alpha in spring 2027 to securities regulators,” with a proposal “to extend the TSX Alpha trading session from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time with a 6 a.m. preopen.” (CEO & Director John McKenzie)

  • McKenzie also cautioned that “extending trading hours is not necessarily for everyone, and it is not without risk,” pointing to “lower liquidity, increased volatility and wider bid-ask spreads” during nontraditional hours. (CEO & Director McKenzie)

  • On capital structure, Arnold said the company remains focused on “positive operating leverage on a full year basis,” referencing “the 6% operating leverage generated in the first 9 months of 2026.” (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

  • Compared with Q2, where TMX disclosed a conservative pro forma leverage peak “up to 3.4x” for pending transactions, Arnold updated that “we expect leverage to probably peak out at slightly less than the 3.4x peak that we mentioned… somewhere in that 3.1x to 3.2x.” (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

Financial Results

  • Revenue of $491.1 million vs. $474,766,670 revenue estimate (analystsEstimates)

  • Arnold said Global Insights posted “26% revenue growth,” with TMX VettaFi revenue “up 46% in Canadian dollars or 44% in U.S. dollars,” and assets under indexing ending the quarter at “USD 309 billion, including $211 billion linked to the RAFI Indices.” (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

  • In Equities and Fixed Income Trading & Clearing, Arnold cited an “8%” revenue increase year-over-year and said combined market share “reached approximately 60%, down 1% year-over-year, but up 1% sequentially from Q2 of 2026.” He also noted that “despite a 9% drop in overall equity volumes, equities trading revenue grew 9%.” (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

  • On costs, Arnold said operating expenses rose “35%” year-over-year, including “$34.1 million of BOX's estimate of higher pass-through costs” tied to the BOX Exchange LLC SRO. He broke this into “approximately $25.9 million” of acquisition/integration and restructuring costs (adjusted from earnings) and “approximately $8.2 million” of higher net pass-through service costs (not adjusted). (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

  • Arnold described liquidity and capital return capacity: TMX ended Q3 with “over $495 million in cash and marketable securities,” and the board approved a dividend of “$0.26 per common share,” with a quarterly payout ratio of “41%” within the “40% to 50%” target range. (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

Q&A

  • Scott Fletcher, CIBC: asked about “aspiration to develop an institutional-grade digital asset infrastructure”; CEO McKenzie said client pain points center on “capital flows, payment flows… collateral mobility,” and described integrating digital capabilities with CDS so clients could “connect to digital networks like the Canton Network” and mobilize collateral from “the $8 trillion in custody.” (CEO & Director John McKenzie)

  • Fletcher, CIBC: asked if urgency changed since last call; McKenzie said “the readiness of the stakeholder group has moved” and that TMX shifted from “more on the research side… and now we're more to the development side and scale up.” (CEO & Director McKenzie)

  • Aravinda Galappatthige, Canaccord: asked about prediction markets and VettaFi organic growth; McKenzie said prediction markets are “not main scale” in Canada, adding, “Our business is in the investing business, it is not in the gambling business,” while describing VettaFi growth as driven by scaling acquired indices, “net new clients,” and “net new products.” (CEO & Director McKenzie)

  • Jaeme Gloyn, National Bank: asked to compare TMX’s strategy with DTCC; McKenzie said TMX is “not at this stage prioritizing the tokenization of individual equities,” focusing instead on “capital flows… fixed income assets, collateral mobility,” and warned tokenizing equities can “fragment[] liquidity.” (CEO & Director McKenzie)

  • Gloyn, National Bank: asked about higher BOX pass-through costs; CFO Arnold said the SRO incurred MEMX-related legal/consulting costs passed through to BOX markets, plus higher estimated SRO service expenses, while stressing “the strategic rationale for the MEMX Group transaction… is unchanged.” (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

  • Stephen Boland, Raymond James: asked about BOX share decline and Trayport subscriber dip; McKenzie said transaction work caused “a substantial distraction impact,” but “we are already seeing some upticks,” and said Trayport subscriber declines can occur quarter-to-quarter and are “a normal piece” of the longer-term trend. (CEO & Director John McKenzie)

  • Bart Dziarski, RBC: asked about buybacks and incremental M&A; Arnold said leverage is expected to peak around “3.1x to 3.2x,” reiterated the 1.5x-2.5x target range, and said the NCIB is “authorized… of 2%,” with execution dependent on “other capital deployment opportunities.” (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

  • Graham Ryding, TD Cowen: asked about Datalinx subscriber growth and AI-related demand; Arnold attributed growth to volatility and said AI workflow demand “isn't vastly pervasive though yet,” while McKenzie added that “investment in Canada is in fashion” and that data demand “is often a lag to the market activity.” (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold; CEO & Director John McKenzie)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst sentiment was slightly positive and exploratory, concentrating on digitization strategy, cost transparency, and acquisition execution; questions such as “can you dig into the higher BOX expenses” reflected scrutiny on expense recurrence. (Jaeme Gloyn, National Bank Financial, Inc.)

  • Management sentiment was positive and promotional in prepared remarks, while measured and risk-aware in Q&A; McKenzie flagged “market quality issues” in extended hours and repeatedly framed digitization as “driven around using that blockchain technology capability integrated with the existing technology.” (CEO & Director John McKenzie)

  • Versus Q2’s heavier emphasis on announcing MEMX Group and pro forma leverage “up to 3.4x,” Q3’s tone leaned more toward integration progress, post-trade digitization, and a narrower leverage range “3.1x to 3.2x,” with less debate around “tokenization” as a near-term threat and more emphasis on practical post-trade use cases. (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold; CEO & Director John McKenzie)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 added closed deals and new bolt-on indexing (TMX Australia Exchange and RAFI Indices closed; SPADE Defense Indices announced post-quarter), while Q2 centered on announcing the MEMX/BOX combination and pending closings for RAFI and “Cboe Australia… close imminently.” (CEO & Director John McKenzie)

  • Q3 introduced a concrete regulatory submission and proposed schedule for TSX Alpha extended hours (“spring 2027”), a topic not detailed in Q2’s transcript. (CEO & Director John McKenzie)

  • Q3’s key investor friction shifted from Q2’s modeling of transaction leverage and private-company disclosure limits toward Q3’s operational questions on BOX pass-through costs, market share softness, and the practical roadmap for digital post-trade modernization. (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold; CEO & Director John McKenzie)

Risks and Concerns

  • McKenzie warned that extended-hours trading can bring “lower liquidity, increased volatility and wider bid-ask spreads,” positioning investor education and regulatory approval as prerequisites. (CEO & Director John McKenzie)

  • Arnold highlighted earnings volatility from “noncash fair value adjustments on foreign exchange hedges” and FX movements tied to acquisitions/intercompany financing, separating reported EPS pressure from “core operating performance” as shown by adjusted EPS growth. (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

  • Management acknowledged BOX-related pass-through cost volatility stemming from the independent SRO structure, with Arnold stating the SRO “operates on a cost recovery basis” and can pass “surplus or deficit to the market.” (Chief Financial Officer David Arnold)

Final Takeaway

TMX management characterized Q3 as a record-revenue quarter driven by Global Insights and derivatives momentum, while emphasizing that reported EPS was pressured by noncash FX-related items. Leadership highlighted active integration of TMX Australia Exchange and RAFI Indices, ongoing regulatory processes for Cboe Canada and MEMX Group, and a proposed spring 2027 launch of extended hours on TSX Alpha alongside explicit warnings on liquidity and volatility risks. In Q&A, executives repeatedly steered digitization toward post-trade collateral mobility and payment frictions—rather than tokenized equities—while also addressing investor scrutiny on BOX’s SRO pass-through costs and keeping capital allocation anchored to returning to the 1.5x-2.5x leverage range after a projected peak around 3.1x-3.2x.

data.title: Mondelez takes a majority stake in Undercover Snacks
data.description:
Mondelez International (MDLZ) became a majority investor in better-for-you snack company Undercover Snacks. 

Undercover Snacks is known for creating delicious treats with healthy ingredients in disguise, including its signature chocolate and frosted quinoa crisps. All Undercover products are non-GMO, certified gluten-free, and produced at the company's dedicated peanut-free, tree-nut-free facility in East Hanover, New Jersey. 

The company began as an entrepreneurial startup and has grown into a nationally recognized brand sold in more than 25K retail locations and enjoyed by millions of travelers each month on United Airlines (UAL). The current distribution network includes grocery, mass, club, drug, foodservice, and e-commerce channels. Its products are sold at leading retailers, including Whole Foods Market, Target, Walmart, Kroger, CVS, Walgreens, Sprouts, and Albertsons, as well as Amazon (AMZN). The company will continue to operate as a standalone business led by its existing management team while gaining access to Mondelez's (MDLZ) extensive capabilities, resources, and expertise to accelerate innovation, distribution, and long-term growth.

data.title: Nasdaq suffers a 3% loss as investors rotate out of technology
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) declined 3% on Friday due to a continued technology rout intensified by Intel’s (INTC) disappointing third-quarter earnings results and other semiconductor positions being sold.

The tech-heavy index is on track for its worst single-day performance since June.

Shares of semiconductor giant Intel (INTC) dropped more than 30% after its third-quarter results showed guidance that missed Wall Street estimates by a considerable margin.

Other semiconductors, including Sandisk (SNDK), CoreWeave (CRWV), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and QUALCOMM (QCOM) also declined more than 10%.

Here are the stocks leading the decline in the Nasdaq:

data.title: Gates anticipates $1.66-$1.72 2026 adjusted EPS while aiming for 6.5% Q4 core growth
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Gates Industrial Corporation Ltd. (GTES) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "In the third quarter, we generated mid-single-digit core sales growth, consistent with our guidance, and delivered strong adjusted EBITDA margin, which approached 24%." (CEO & Director Ivo Jurek)
  • "Given our performance year-to-date and current demand trends, we are raising our full year adjusted earnings per share guidance." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "Third quarter sales were approximately $904 million" and "Adjusted EBITDA margin increased 90 basis points to a company record of 23.8%." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "In Power Transmission, sales were approximately $560 million" with "adjusted EBITDA margin of 24.5%." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "In Fluid Power, sales were approximately $343 million" and "Our data center revenues increased about 2.5x compared to the last year's third quarter." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "Adjusted EPS increased from $0.39 per share in the prior year quarter to a record $0.47 per share." (Executive VP & CFO L. Mallard)

Outlook

  • "We have narrowed our full year core sales growth to a range of 3.2% to 3.8%" and "We now anticipate full year adjusted EBITDA to be in the range of $809 million to $823 million." (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • "We have updated our full year adjusted earnings per share to a range of $1.66 per share to $1.72 per share" and "For the fourth quarter, we estimate total sales to be in the range of $905 million to $925 million and core revenue growth to be approximately 6.5% at the midpoint." (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • "We are reiterating our expectation for second half core sales growth to approximately 6% at the midpoint as well as second half adjusted EBITDA margin to measure approximately 23.5%." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • Compared with Q2, management shifted from raising full-year core-sales-growth guidance to "maintaining the 3.5% midpoint" while increasing adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS ranges. (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)

Financial Results

  • "Third quarter sales were approximately $904 million" with "core growth of 5.5%." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "Adjusted EBITDA was $215 million" and "Adjusted earnings per share increased approximately 21% to a quarterly record of $0.47." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "Our trailing 12-month free cash flow conversion was 82%" and "Our net leverage ratio ended the quarter at 1.8x." (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • "We repurchased approximately $57 million worth of our shares in the third quarter" and "Our return on invested capital was 21.5% on a trailing 12-month basis." (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)

Q&A

  • Stephen Volkmann, Jefferies: asked why Q4 margin steps down with faster growth; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "we do see some normal seasonality," plus "a little bit of dilution from a price/cost perspective" and "a significant increase in our variable comp... mostly hits in Q4."
  • Stephen Volkmann, Jefferies: asked about M&A valuations; CEO & Director Jurek: "we're going to be very disciplined" and "we will do deals" that "generate appropriate returns" and "be accretive."
  • Jeffrey Hammond, KeyBanc: asked about price/cost differences between segments; CEO & Director Jurek: "we are making bigger investments" and said FP is performing "absent" investment effects.
  • Nigel Coe, Wolfe: asked early view on 2027; CEO & Director Jurek: "the setup is really developing quite nicely" and said the company will outline 2027 thinking on "November 19."
  • Nigel Coe, Wolfe: asked data center product pipeline and inventory pickup; CEO & Director Jurek: "pretty significant increase in the product launches" across "hoses... pumps... coupling"; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: inventory includes "safety stock" and said pricing collection supports confidence in "90-plus percent conversion number."
  • Jeffrey Hammond, KeyBanc: asked North America drags and auto trends; CEO & Director Jurek: "auto OE was down slightly" and "AR was up slightly" while industrial OEM growth was "in the 20s" and industrial aftermarket accelerated "into the low teens."
  • Andrew Kaplowitz, Citi: asked about enterprise initiatives 2.0; CEO & Director Jurek: "we will certainly provide you a window" but "much more focusing on delivering above-market growth rate"; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "we are super focused on growth as we move forward."
  • Andrew Kaplowitz, Citi: asked personal mobility visibility; CEO & Director Jurek: "We have a terrific visibility" and said trajectory is "driving that 20% to 30% growth rate."
  • Tomohiko Sano, JPMorgan: asked data center right-to-win and engagement; CEO & Director Jurek: referenced "production ramp-up of our e-water pumps" and working with "a couple of hyperscalers" and "infrastructure builders."
  • Tomohiko Sano, JPMorgan: asked NPI/R&D allocation; CEO & Director Jurek: "we've made some anticipated expectations that we're going to get into the low 20s in NPI vitality."
  • David Raso, Evercore: asked off-highway/customer inventory and pricing; CEO & Director Jurek: off-highway was "somewhat mixed" with construction strength and ag "flattish to maybe just slightly down"; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "our 80/20 tools" are improving "analytical pricing."
  • David Raso, Evercore: asked variable comp drag uniqueness; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "this year is a little bit more normalized" and last year "lower than normal"; CEO & Director Jurek: "we are printing record results."
  • Jerry Revich, Wells Fargo: asked implied Q4 margin headwinds; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: watch "more dilutive... price/cost" as "higher-cost inventory continues to move through."
  • Jerry Revich, Wells Fargo: asked margin upside beyond 2027 targets; CEO & Director Jurek: margin upside comes from "enterprise initiatives" plus "a nice component of volume."
  • Christopher Dankert, D.A. Davidson: asked about the belts acquisition; CEO & Director Jurek: closed "beginning of Q4" with "diminutive" Q4 revenue, "more meaningful" in 2027 at "about 100 bps, plus or minus" of revenue, and profitability "dilutive" initially with a plan to reach "company average profitability" in "the next 12 months."
  • Brandon Knutson, Morgan Stanley: asked personal mobility acceleration and capacity for mobility/data center; CEO & Director Jurek: mobility growth was "broad-based" and capacity is "in place"; for data center, "We are investing in R&D... production scale-up... adding capacity."
  • Brandon Knutson, Morgan Stanley: asked to quantify growth investments; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "we don't really quantify the different pieces and the parts."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly skeptical on near-term margins, cash/inventory, and the Q4 guide framing, including "margin stepping down" (Stephen Volkmann, Jefferies) and "beatable implied 4Q guide" (Jerry Revich, Wells Fargo).
  • Management tone was slightly positive and forward-leaning on growth, repeatedly pointing to durability and optionality, including "the setup is really developing quite nicely" (CEO & Director Jurek) and "significant optionality to deploy capital" (Executive VP & CFO Mallard).
  • Versus Q2, management confidence language shifted from "early stages of an industrial recovery" to acceleration, including "Relative to the second quarter, our industrial core growth accelerated" (CEO & Director Jurek) and a clearer tilt toward "strategic inorganic investments." (CEO & Director Jurek)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 emphasized acceleration and North America inflection, including "North America inflected positively" and "industrial core growth accelerated to high single digits from mid-single digits." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • Q2 focused on entering recovery and raising broad guidance, including "we believe that we have entered the early stages of an industrial recovery" and "we have raised our 2026 full year guidance for core sales growth and profitability." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • Q3 guidance changes were more targeted: "maintaining the 3.5% midpoint" core-sales-growth outlook while increasing adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS ranges, compared with Q2 raising core-sales-growth, EBITDA, and EPS guidance together. (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • Analyst focus shifted from ERP and pricing mechanics in Q2 to Q4 margin cadence, inventories, M&A, and integration of the belts acquisition in Q3.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Some normal seasonality" and "less working days" were cited as Q4 margin headwinds, alongside "a little bit of dilution from a price/cost perspective" and a Q4 "variable comp" step-up. (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • Management pointed to end-market mix risk, noting North America "auto OE was down slightly" and agriculture remained weak, described as "flattish to maybe just slightly down" in Q3. (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • On the belts acquisition, management flagged near-term profitability dilution, saying profitability "was dilutive" and requires execution to reach "company average profitability" within "the next 12 months." (CEO & Director Jurek)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as a quarter of accelerating industrial demand, record profitability metrics, and a stronger North America trend, while raising full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.66-$1.72 and holding the full-year core-sales-growth midpoint at 3.5%. Executives highlighted ongoing investments in data centers and personal mobility, a more active interest in disciplined M&A, and a newly closed belts acquisition expected to contribute more meaningfully in 2027, with margin seasonality, price/cost normalization, and variable compensation identified as key drivers shaping Q4 profitability cadence.

data.title: Rio Tinto begins restart of Oyu Tolgoi underground operations after seismic event
data.description:
Rio Tinto (RIO) said Friday it is progressively restarting underground operations at the Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia after completing safety reviews following a seismic event that ​temporarily halted mining activities.

Rio (RIO) said ​a seismic event triggered ⁠a localized rockfall in a temporary storage ​area adjacent to the production zone, causing ​ground vibrations but resulting in no structural damage to the underground cave or operating infrastructure; two employees continue to receive treatment for non-life-threatening injuries.

The company has been ramping up underground mining at Oyu Tolgoi, where open-pit operations began in 2011, but the most valuable copper resources lie underground.

A pause on underground operations at Oyu Tolgoi is unlikely to have a long-term impact on the project's production, but "a core question that this event generates is, 'What is the long-term sustainable rate of cave propagation, and does it align with the targeted production rate?" Jefferies analysts said in a note.

The Oyu Tolgoi underground uses block caving, a process that stresses the surrounding rock, and Jefferies wonders whether such events could change the way investors value different mining techniques.

"For those generalists not frightened from the sector by mining disruptions, we do think that we will start to see further premiums paid for lower-risk mining methods," the bank wrote.

Rio (RIO) owns a 66% stake in Oyu Tolgoi, one ​of the world's largest known copper ​and gold deposits, with the Mongolian government holding the rest.

data.title: Cracks in the cart: Consumer staples hit a wall as inflation outpaces sales
data.description:
The narrative of the “resilient consumer” is breaking down as major consumer staples (XLP) companies increasingly deliver organic revenue growth that lags the pace of inflation, according to Sakonnet Research.

While packaged goods giants posted organic sales growth between 7% and 9% across North America in 2022 and early 2023, the pace slowed considerably once pricing actions peaked and volumes softened, analyst Adam Josephson noted.

By 2024 and 2025, average organic growth across the sector flattened to near zero.

Through the first three quarters of 2026, that weakness has solidified. Average organic sales across 20 staples manufacturers grew by just 2% in the first quarter and decelerated to 1% in both the second and third quarters.

While several beverage and personal care brands such as Coca-Cola (KO), Procter & Gamble (PG), and Church & Dwight (CHD) maintained modest gains, packaged food manufacturers—including General Mills (GIS), Kraft Heinz (KHC), Conagra (CAG), and Campbell's (CPB)—recorded recurring contractions in their North American business.

On the inflation front, the Consumer Price Index advanced 3.7% Y/Y in September as energy costs surged. The core CPI measure, which strips out volatile food and energy costs, grew 2.6% from a year ago and remains above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.

data.title: U.S. Department of Justice said to be aware of Binance hack reports
data.description:
U.S. Department of Justice is aware of the reports surrounding the Binance hack, and the Secret Service is investigating the matter with private-sector partners, including Circle (CRCL), Bloomberg News reported, citing an emailed statement.

Secret Service is looking to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds stolen from Binance, according to the statement.

Separately, a person familiar with the situation told Reuters that Binance is ‌working with law enforcement around the world, including the Federal ​Bureau of Investigation.

The theft of $6.3B of assets from Binance, constituting the world's largest crypto hack, was conducted by a North Korean cybercrime group, according to two crypto analysis firms' assessment.

The world's largest crypto exchange had frozen about $3B of its $6.3B in assets affected by a massive hack, and was expecting to freeze more. At about noon, Binance said withdrawals are expected to resume within the next 42 hours.

The attack, which took place on Thursday, started with a compromised laptop belonging to an employee. Binance's investigation identified additional points of breach, indicating the incident went beyond one device.

The exchange didn't find any evidence that wallet private keys were compromised. The company assured that its users won't bear any losses. "All losses will be covered in full by its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds," it said.

Crypto stocks were trading lower after the news: Coinbase Global (COIN) -13.34% to $139.16; Hut 8 (HUT) -13.18% to $57.68; Bullish (BLSH) -12.05% to $25.04; Cipher Digital (CIFR) -12.04% to $7.13; IREN (IREN) -10.32% to $23.54; Bakkt (BKKT) -10.24% to $4.56; and Riot Platforms (RIOT) -10.08% to $12.36.

data.title: Anthropic may get junk credit rating after its IPO, Blackstone says: report
data.description:
• Anthropic (ANT) may receive a high-yield, or junk, credit rating after its IPO, which can complicate the AI company's plans to borrow money to fund its growing infrastructure spending, according to a media report. 
  • Blackstone (BX), an anchor investor in Anthropic's $63B chip financing deal known as Project North Star, has told investors that the company is more likely to receive a rating in the double-B range or higher, according to the Financial Times report.
  • An investment-grade rating would allow Anthropic to borrow at lower costs to finance its artificial intelligence infrastructure projects.
  • Anthropic has more than $112B in cash and equivalents, while investors expect the company could raise about $100B through its IPO, the report said.

data.title: ‘Don’t rule out further drawdowns’ in tech as current cycle hits 22 drawdowns in only two years – Turning Point Market Research
data.description:
The technology sectors have already seen 22 drawdowns in performance since 2024, while the 1995-2000 tech bubble had 36 in total, according to Turning Point Market Research analysts.

Currently, the average public tech stock is down 37.1% from its 52-week high, due to the ongoing sell-off across AI stocks (AIQ), semiconductors (SMH), (XSD), and the overall technology sector (XLK), (VGT).

From 1995 to 2000, technology sub-industries experienced 36 independent drawdowns of 20% or more, compared with 22 since 2024, Turning Point Market Research analysts noted.

Within the technology sub-industries, internet services and infrastructure saw 10 drawdowns between 1995 and 2000, and only one from 2024 until now.

The biggest drawdowns in the past two years were in electronic components and semiconductors. Each sub-sector saw three.

The deepest drawdown in recent years in semiconductors (SMH), (XSD) was -35.1%.

 

 

 

“With that in mind, don't rule out further, potentially more painful drawdowns,” Turning Point analysts said. “Drawdowns are a common feature of major innovation cycles.”
